title: topology-img-core: a preregistered study of topological crossover and finite-size nonconvergence in task detectability
description:
A preregistered study relating persistent homology of noisy images to task detectability. A fixed Gaussian lesion is embedded in a uniform field and degraded only by additive white Gaussian noise — no correlated noise, no blur, no reconstruction physics — and topology is evaluated by a superlevel cubical filtration with H0 and H1 reported separately, against an ideal prewhitening observer.

This archive accompanies the manuscript Topology and Task Detectability in Synthetic Phantoms: A Preregistered Study of Nonlinear Crossover and Finite-Size Nonconvergence. It contains the Phase-0 noise sweep, the unpaired two-sample validation, the seed-sensitivity measurement, the refined sigma grids at matrix sizes 64, 96, 128, 192 and 256, the resource-gate calibration, and the finite-size scaling analysis, together with the scripts that produce them.

The preregistration is verifiable, not merely asserted. The freeze commit precedes the first data commit and continuous integration asserts that it is an ancestor of it, so the registered design cannot have been written after the data it governs.

The preregistered classification of the finite-size result is Outcome 3, nonconvergence over the reachable range of image sizes. The nonlinear topological crossover reproduces; its location does not converge over N = 64 to 256 under the registered criteria. No imaging data of any kind is used or redistributed: every image analysed is generated by the code in this archive.
